# Implement block: Pill Rise Splash (React Native)

You are adding the "Pill Rise Splash" block from Native Cook to the user's React Native app. The block already exists as working code. Your job is to bring it into this project faithfully, not to write a new one that looks similar.

## The block

A flat lime splash with a dark green mark in the middle: two slanted bars passing each other. A dark capsule peeks up from the bottom edge holding a round lime button with an arrow, rises as a tall pill filled with an iridescent swirl, then widens into the whole screen and pushes the mark up and away. The swirl darkens into an onboarding board: a thin three-step progress bar, three glazed jars painted in red, yellow and marbled blue floating at different tilts, gold coins spinning above them and dropping into their mouths, the headline "90 COUNTRIES, 30 CURRENCIES. ONE WALLET" in a heavy condensed face, a lime "See our rates" link and a full-width lime "Get started" button. Pressing the button grows it into a full lime screen and the mark fades back in.

**Motion.** One progress value drives the splash: from 0 the capsule (68 pt wide) peeks with its button 64 pt above the home indicator (0.12, 520 ms ease-out (0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)), rises to 30% of the screen height (0.48), touches the top while widening to 1.8 times its width with 61 pt corners (0.68), and fills the screen with corners closing from 46 pt to 0 (1). The swirl inside is fixed to the screen and settles from 120% to 100% scale; a dark cap at the capsule's top fades out by 0.46; the button rides the capsule's top, then lifts 110 pt and fades between 0.48 and 0.68. The capsule's top pushes the mark up as it passes and the mark fades over 130 pt of push. The board then enters over 1.4 s (linear progress, after 120 ms): the dark backdrop fades in over its first half, the three headline lines rise out of clipped baselines one by one (8% apart, each over 38%, ease-out), the jars rise 46 pt and grow from 84% to 100% one after another (9% apart), the button slides up 90 pt and the first progress segment fills. Each jar bobs 6 pt on its own period (3.1, 3.6 and 3.3 s) and sways 0.025 rad. A coin appears above a jar, spins about its horizontal axis at 7 rad/s while it sinks 8 pt for 0.32 s, then falls with a gravity of 1900 pt/s² into the mouth, steering onto its centre, and disappears behind the near rim; the jar dips up to 7 pt in a ringing spring (19 rad/s, decaying at 6/s) and squashes slightly. Dragging up on the splash moves the capsule with the finger (a screen of travel is 0.85 of the progress) with resistance below the peek; a release that would pass 0.42 within 0.22 s of its speed opens it with a critically damped spring (1300 ms, overshoot clamped) carrying the finger's speed, otherwise it springs back to the peek (450 ms, damping ratio 0.8). A tap anywhere on the splash also opens it. On the board a jar can be dragged (past 160 pt it gives at 30%), tilting up to 0.4 rad with the finger's sideways speed, and springs home with the release speed (stiffness 220, damping 13 per unit mass, so it wobbles); a tap drops a coin into the nearest jar. Pressing the button scales it to 97% for 110 ms, then it opens into a full-screen lime rectangle over 650 ms (ease-in-out (0.77, 0, 0.175, 1)), everything resets under it and the mark fades and grows back in over 520 ms. A light haptic marks the capsule opening, each coin a finger dropped landing, and the button press. The self-playing demo peeks at 0.6 s, opens at 1.4 s (1.5 s, ease-in-out (0.6, 0, 0.3, 1)), drops coins at 4.5, 5.25, 5.95, 6.7 and 7.4 s, presses the button at 9.0 s, is back on the resting splash at 10.35 s and repeats every 11 s. A touch pauses it for 4 s; it then picks up at the matching point of the loop. Under reduced motion the demo does not play, the capsule stays at its peek and the swirl crossfades in over 420 ms, the jars do not bob or rise, coins fade in and out at the mouth instead of falling, and the button's way back is a 300 ms crossfade.

## Reference source

The block is built and running in the Native Cook source repository. Each link below is a file on GitHub. To read one as plain text, replace `https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/` with `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/` in its address.

### Demo (start here)

- [index.tsx](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/src/blocks/splash/pill-rise-splash/index.tsx)

### Files of the block

- [PillRiseJar.tsx](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/src/blocks/splash/pill-rise-splash/PillRiseJar.tsx)
- [PillRiseSplash.tsx](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/src/blocks/splash/pill-rise-splash/PillRiseSplash.tsx)

### Packages

- `@shopify/react-native-skia`
- `expo-haptics`
- `expo-status-bar`
- `react-native-gesture-handler`
- `react-native-reanimated`
- `react-native-safe-area-context`
- `react-native-worklets`

The versions the block was built with are in [react-native/package.json](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/package.json).

## Your instructions

_Anything specific to this app goes here: where the block should appear, what to rename, what to change. Left empty, integrate the block as it is._

## How to work

Work like an experienced React Native engineer joining an existing project: learn the app first, read only what you need, decide early how the block fits, then integrate it with as little disruption as possible. Take the steps in order.

**Done means** the block is reachable in the user's app and behaves like the reference on iOS or Android: a simulator, an emulator or a device. A browser is never proof. Do not open the app on the web to check it, not even when the mobile build fails.

**Fidelity.** Bring over the real implementation. Keep its structure, colours, sizes, timings and easing. Change only what this project requires and what "Your instructions" ask for.

If you already learned this project earlier in the conversation, reuse what you know and skip step 2. Learn it again only if the project changed or something you need is missing.

### 1. Check where you are

- You need the project's files and a terminal. If this prompt was pasted into a chat that has neither, stop and say so: it has to be run by a coding agent opened on the project.
- Confirm the project is a React Native app, Expo or bare. If it is something else, stop, say what you found, and do not create a new app inside it unless the instructions ask for one.

### 2. Learn the host app

- Expo (managed or prebuild) or bare React Native, and the versions of React Native and the Expo SDK.
- The package manager, and how the app is started: Expo Go, a development build, or `react-native run-ios` / `run-android`.
- Navigation: Expo Router, React Navigation, something else, or a single screen. Find how a screen is added today.
- Conventions: TypeScript or not, path aliases, how styles are written, where components and screens live.
- Which of the block's packages are already installed, and at which versions.

### 3. Read the block

- Open the demo, then each file it imports. The list above names every file of the block, so you do not have to guess.
- The demo is how the source repository shows the block. Bring over what the demo renders, not the repository's gallery. Anything listed under "Used by the demo only" stays behind.
- Read the block's props and their defaults. The demo may switch on an option that makes the block play by itself for a recording (for example `autoPlay`). Keep the option; leave it off in the user's app unless asked.

### 4. Decide the fit

- Compare the block's packages with the host's. Install what is missing with the project's own tool (`npx expo install …` in an Expo app, so versions match its SDK).
- A package with native code needs a new native build, and Expo Go only runs the modules it ships with. Say so before you install one, and say which build the user will need.
- If the host is on older versions and an API differs, adapt the block's code to the host. Do not upgrade the host's React Native, Expo SDK or animation libraries without asking.
- Put the files where this app keeps its components. Ask only when two places are equally reasonable and the choice matters.

### 5. Bring it in

- Copy the block's files, keep their names, and rewrite imports to this project's paths and aliases.
- Copy its images and fonts with it, and load fonts the way the project already does.
- Keep reduced-motion handling, haptics and accessibility labels as they are in the source.
- Mount the block where the instructions say. With no instructions, add a screen or route named after the block and make it reachable the way the app's other screens are.

### 6. Run it

- Typecheck and lint with the project's own commands and fix what the block introduced.
- Run the app on the user's usual mobile target and use the block: every state, every gesture, and once with reduced motion on.
- If the simulator, the emulator or the native build fails, report the error and ask how to continue. Do not fall back to the web.

### 7. Report

- Files added and changed, packages installed, and whether a new native build is needed.
- How to reach the block in the app.
- Anything that differs from the reference, and why.
